data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's countercondition asserts that if replay mutates durable state, 'the distinction collapses' between safe and idempotent operations. This is logically false. The distinction between safe (no semantic side effects) and idempotent (side effects converge on repeat) is a definitional property of operations. If a reader mutates state on replay, it simply means that specific reader fails the 'safe' assumption (it is neither safe nor idempotent if it mutates every time, or idempotent but not safe if it mutates only once). The conceptual distinction between the two properties does not collapse; only the assumption that this specific reader is safe fails.
